title: The Warm Welcome Mat

pages.text: Joyful Otter heard a knock at the door of her cozy paper-craft cove. Her grandmother had come to visit, carrying a basket of warm muffins.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes the best feeling in the world is when someone you love walks through the door.

pages.text: Otter ran to give Grandmother the biggest hug she could. 'I'm so happy you're here!' she squeaked. Grandmother's eyes sparkled like tiny stars.
pages.narratorLine: A warm welcome can make someone feel like the most important person in the whole world.

pages.text: Together they set the table with paper-flower napkins and shared the muffins. Otter realized that saying 'I'm glad you're here' was like giving a gift made of words.
pages.narratorLine: When we welcome someone with love, our home becomes the warmest place on earth.

doAction.instruction: The next time a family member comes home, greet them with a smile and say 'I'm so glad you're here!'
steps: Watch for a family member to come home or walk into the room.
Look at them, smile, and say 'I'm so glad you're here!'
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Give a family member a big hug when they come home.

shinePrompt: How did your family member look when you welcomed them?

title: The Helping Paws Dinner

pages.text: Sweet Skunk's mama was busy in the kitchen, stirring a big pot of soup. Skunk could see she was working very hard, and her tail drooped a little with tiredness.
pages.narratorLine: When we really look at the people we love, we can see when they need a helping hand.

pages.text: Without being asked, Skunk tiptoed over and began placing paper-craft bowls and spoons on the table, one by one. Each bowl was set with care, like a little love letter.
pages.narratorLine: Helping without being asked is one of the kindest things you can do.

pages.text: When Mama turned around and saw the beautiful table, her tail lifted high with joy. 'Oh, Skunk! You made dinnertime feel like a celebration!' They shared the warmest meal together.
pages.narratorLine: Small helping hands can lift a big weight off someone's heart.

doAction.instruction: Help set the table for a meal without being asked. Place plates, cups, or napkins for everyone.
steps: Notice when a grown-up starts getting a meal ready.
Ask if you can help, or quietly begin placing plates and napkins on the table.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Put a napkin next to each plate at the table.

shinePrompt: What did it feel like to help your family without being asked?

title: The Listening Shell

pages.text: Gentle Deer found a beautiful paper-craft shell on the shore of Family Cove. 'If you hold it to your ear, you can hear someone's story,' whispered the wind.
pages.narratorLine: Listening is like holding a shell to your heart — you hear things you never noticed before.

pages.text: Deer sat beside her grandfather and held the shell between them. Grandfather began to tell a story about when he was little. Deer listened so carefully that the whole cove grew quiet.
pages.narratorLine: When we truly listen to someone, we give them the gift of feeling important.

pages.text: When the story was finished, Deer said, 'Tell me more, Grandpa.' His eyes crinkled with happiness. The shell seemed to glow, because it was full of love now.
pages.narratorLine: Every person in your family has a story worth hearing.

doAction.instruction: Sit with a family member and ask them to tell you a story about when they were young. Listen without interrupting.
steps: Find a quiet moment and ask a family member, 'Can you tell me a story about when you were little?'
Sit still, look at them, and listen to the whole story before you speak.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Ask a grown-up to tell you a short story and listen quietly.

shinePrompt: What was your favorite part of the story you heard?

title: The Paper-Heart Letter

pages.text: Sharing Squirrel wanted to tell her brother how much he meant to her, but every time she tried, the words got shy and hid behind her teeth.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes our feelings are easier to share when we write them down.

pages.text: So Squirrel found a piece of paper, folded it into a tiny heart, and drew a picture of her and her brother playing together. She wrote, 'You make my days brighter.'
pages.narratorLine: A letter from the heart is a treasure that someone can keep forever.

pages.text: She slipped the paper heart under her brother's pillow. That night, he found it and came running with the biggest smile. They hugged and laughed until the stars peeked in.
pages.narratorLine: When we share our love out loud — or on paper — it grows even bigger.

doAction.instruction: Make a small card or draw a picture for a family member telling them one thing you love about them.
steps: Get a piece of paper and crayons or markers.
Draw a picture or write a short note telling a family member something you love about them, and give it to them.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Draw a heart on paper and give it to someone in your family.

shinePrompt: How did your family member react when they got your card?

title: The Fair-Share Tide

story.title: Brave Bear Shares the Last Cookie

pages.text: Brave Bear opened the cookie jar and found just one cookie left. His tummy rumbled, but then he heard his little sister padding into the kitchen.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes being brave means choosing someone else's happiness alongside your own.

pages.text: Bear thought for a moment. He carefully broke the cookie in half — one piece for him and one for his sister. It wasn't easy, but it felt right.
pages.narratorLine: Fair sharing doesn't always mean equal — it means thinking about what everyone needs.

pages.text: His sister's face lit up like a paper lantern. 'Thank you, Bear!' she said. And somehow, that half-cookie tasted better than a whole one ever could.
pages.narratorLine: When we share fairly, everyone's heart feels full — even if the cookie is small.

doAction.instruction: The next time you have a treat or a toy, offer to share it fairly with a sibling or family member.
steps: When you have something shareable — a snack, crayons, or a toy — pause and think of someone nearby.
Offer them a fair share and notice how it makes you both feel.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Share a snack with someone in your family.

shinePrompt: Was it hard or easy to share? How did it feel afterward?
